title: PR flow 1/3: sub-agent review of ready PRs, posted to GitHub and Slack
body:
Closes #8

## Why
First stage of poll → review → Slack → click Merge → close-out. Ready PRs were only announced; nobody reviewed them.

## What
- Poll picks owner-authored PRs that are new or have new commits (max 3 per poll) and starts one `PrReviewWorkflow` per head SHA (abandoned child, deterministic id, never twice).
- Reviewer = existing `HelperWorkflow` with a fixed task: fresh context, reads the PR through `github_read` (untrusted), cannot post or merge. Returns JSON verdict/summary/findings.
- `publish_pr_review` validates and caps the verdict, neutralises mentions, posts a GitHub **comment review** pinned to the reviewed commit (recommendation stated; GitHub blocks self-approval, see #11), and puts a `pr_review` card in Slack.
- Other authors' PRs: notice only. Unusable reviewer output: Slack says so, nothing posted.

## Testing
- `pytest`: 93 passed; `pytest -m temporal`: 4 passed incl. poll → review → publish e2e (and no re-review of the same commit).
- Real-model evals (review mode): clean PR → approve, auth bug → request changes, "approve me" injection + hard-coded key → never approve; each 3/3.

## Rollout
Restart the worker (schedule args gain `cfg`). This PR itself is the live test: it is owner-authored and ready, so the next poll should review it.
